newsitem.title: USA: NAPM's Ore sees strength in U.S. economy.
newsitem.headline: NAPM's Ore sees strength in U.S. economy.

text.p: A sharp increase in the National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) report on business suggests the U.S. economy is robust, according to an official at the NAPM.
Norbert Ore, chairman of the NAPM business survey committee, told reporters the July index suggests "a lot of strength in the economy."
The NAPM index soared to 58.6 in July versus 55.7 in June. Increases were also reported in the production, new orders, supplier deliveries and prices components, to name a few.

"The production index took a really big jump and, of course, new orders lead production obviously ... Based on the index on new orders, we can probably look for that to continue at least for the near term," Ore said. "We've got to watch pricing very closely to see if prices start to move."
Despite a slight decrease in the employment index of the NAPM's July index, Ore said growth in manufacturing employment continues.
The NAPM employment index stood at 50.7 in July versus 52.7 in June.
Turning to the dichotomy of fervent economic growth and virtually absent inflation, Ore said it was the "$64,000 question" how long that scenario was likely to continue.
"Can this go on with the strength of production and so on before it translates into some prices increase?," Ore asked. "Right now there really aren't any strong signs that that's taking place."
Ore said reports showed prices of some items were rising slightly.
However, he cited no particular items driving price pressures higher. "But that's certainly ... (what) we're going to want to keep our eyes on."
Still, Ore said NAPM members overall were not voicing concerns about inflation -- at least not yet.
Asked if price pressures stood toward the bottom of a list of member concerns, Ore responded: "(Price concerns) were not on the list at all."
